merger_name: Advent Partners – investment in Procare Group

merger_description:
Advent Partners 4 Fund, LP (**Advent Partners**) proposes to acquire the majority indirect interest in Procare Group Pty Ltd (**Procare**).  

  

Advent Partners is a Melbourne-based private capital investor that invests in and manages a portfolio of businesses across a range of sectors including healthcare, consumer, education, technology and software.   

  

Procare is a diversified insurance support services group supplying services to insurers, underwriters, and brokers across Australia. Its key services include loss adjusting, factual and surveillance investigations, injury management, recoveries, forensic accounting and fraud, legal services (via PC Legal Pty Ltd), claims management and consulting, workers’ compensation & investigations training (via a registered training organisation), claims and risk services (via Procare Claims & Risk Pty Ltd), cyber incident response (via Procare Cyber Pty Ltd), and rehabilitation and NDIS services (via PC Ability Pty Ltd).   

  

AUB Group Limited (**AUB**), an ASX-listed entity which is comprised of insurance brokers and underwriting agencies, currently owns ~48% of Procare. Management and employees of Procare currently own (directly or indirectly) the balance of Procare.   

  

On completion of the transaction, existing management and employee shareholders of Procare will retain the remaining minority indirect interest in Procare, and AUB will not hold any interest.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is a very small horizontal overlap between Advent
Partners and Procare in the supply of cyber security services
b. there are alternative suppliers of cyber security services in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
